design_decisions: Source-health state is not stored on event occurrences; source fetch/parser incidents live in a separate monitor ledger.
Conditional activation has explicit state and trigger-evidence fields.
Occurrence identity remains immutable across date/time/location/status changes.
Calendar render policy is derived from canonical fields and not treated as temporal truth.
Time precision and time certainty are distinct: clock-time claims record both time_status and time_basis.
A scheduled statistical release occurrence is distinct from the data vintage(s) published at that occurrence.
One release occurrence may publish multiple data products at the same timestamp; those products are represented in data_products[] rather than duplicated calendar events.
Source-specific estimate/revision labels are preserved verbatim while a normalized release_stage_class supports cross-jurisdiction analysis.
Reference periods belong primarily to individual data products; occurrence-level reference_period is only a convenience summary.
No future release occurrence may be generated beyond an authoritative schedule horizon solely from historical recurrence.
Canonical identity and calendar display aggregation are separate concerns.
Independent official releases that share a timestamp retain separate occurrence_ids; the renderer may cluster them for human readability.
A SOURCE_BUNDLE is one actual publication occurrence containing multiple data products. A RENDER_CLUSTER is a presentation grouping of independent canonical occurrences.
Render clustering must never merge provenance, lifecycle, cancellation state or change history between member occurrences.
Canonical registry inclusion does not imply default calendar visibility.
visibility_tier controls human-facing density independently of intrinsic importance and expected market sensitivity.
Sovereign auction occurrences represent the auction/tender operation; announcement, result and settlement timestamps are related milestones unless analytically useful as separate occurrences.
An indicative issuance calendar creates a PROVISIONAL occurrence; a later instrument-specific tender announcement may upgrade that same occurrence to CONFIRMED.
A legal/fiscal civil-date boundary is not necessarily a clock-time event and may legitimately have no IANA timezone.
Funding expiry, legal publication deadline, fiscal-year boundary, negotiation deadline and conditional lapse risk are distinct deadline types.
A politically contingent risk is linked to its deterministic boundary but is not inferred to occur merely because the boundary exists.
A bill-specified future deadline can be stored before enactment only as conditional on enactment; enactment upgrades activation state rather than creating a new occurrence.
TBC fiscal publications may carry a legal latest date without that latest date being misrepresented as the publication date.
Source authority, technical accessibility and legal/licensing permission are separate dimensions.
An authoritative source may be registered but held out of canonical ingestion where its terms restrict database population, automated use, redistribution or AI/ML use.
Actual exchange/index mechanics may be recorded without promoting market folklore labels into predictive signals.
Rule-derived derivatives expiries may be canonical where the exchange contract specification itself defines the rule.
Market-session semantics such as after-close are retained as semantic times; no arbitrary clock time is invented.
Settlement-cycle regime changes are policy/market-structure implementation events and remain distinct from daily settlement observations.
source_id is immutable and globally unique. A new endpoint must never reuse an existing source_id even for the same institution.
Automated audit prose must derive its gate verdict from machine validation; a hard-coded PASS/FAIL narrative is forbidden.
Standing institutional identity is separate from rotating presidency/host-year source authority.
A host_year_binding links an institution/year to the authoritative chair or host source without replacing the institution's standing source.
Host certainty and event-date certainty are orthogonal: a host year can be confirmed while timing remains TBC.
Month-only summit information is preserved at MONTH precision as a bounded window; no representative day is invented.
An official meeting-date change updates one immutable occurrence and retains both authoritative assertions in the change ledger.
Rule-mandated annual institutional meetings may have an undated TBC occurrence where existence is authoritative but timing is not.
Source freshness affects monitoring priority: old official governance resolutions may support provisional future records but require elevated reverification.
A later, more precise authoritative schedule upgrades the existing occurrence rather than creating a new one.
Date-status can move from EXPECTED_WINDOW/PROVISIONAL to an exact confirmed multi-day occurrence while preserving the earlier assertion and precision state.
Cross-institutional events held alongside another summit remain separate canonical series: East Asia Summit is not an ASEAN Summit subrecord.
An institution may have an annual/high-level event confirmed for a year or month without a specific day; year/month precision is preserved.
High-level institutional calendars require noise control: only events with a defensible political, economic, security, climate, health or systemic-governance transmission channel enter Tier 1.
Temporal precision and certainty are orthogonal. An officially announced month-only event can be CONFIRMED while retaining MONTH precision.
A colloquial political process grouping (for example China's 'Two Sessions') must not collapse legally distinct NPC and CPPCC sessions into one canonical occurrence.
A non-canonical anticipatory_monitor may use historical/customary patterns to decide when to intensify source checking, but it is never itself an event assertion or calendar record.
Rule-derived future dates requiring a holiday/workday adjustment must preserve the complete derivation chain and all authoritative rule/input sources.
Late-announced policy processes such as the Central Economic Work Conference remain in the Source/Change Monitor until authoritative timing is published.

Policy-document streams such as 15th Five-Year Plan sector plans are monitored as document flows; only publications with a distinct material implementation date or decision point become calendar occurrences.
Independent statistical releases sharing one timestamp retain separate occurrence identities and may be grouped only through a render_cluster.
An election_process is a stable political cycle containing multiple milestone occurrences; polling day is not the process identity.
Election process groups and milestone occurrences are separate canonical objects.
First-round, runoff/second-round, result declaration, certification/diplomation, inauguration and government formation have different activation semantics.
A second round may have an exact calendar date while remaining conditionally inactive until the first-round outcome triggers it.
A constitutionally rule-derived polling day is canonical when the legal rule uniquely determines the date; the derivation chain must be retained.
A legally required result or certification deadline is not misrepresented as the actual declaration/certification timestamp.
Government formation and coalition formation are live political processes unless a legal timetable creates a canonical deadline.
An election date can move because electoral law changes; the same process/milestone identity is preserved and the superseded schedule remains in the change ledger.
A date can be politically announced before being legally proclaimed; legal activation/proclamation status is separate from date certainty.
Callable/snap elections with no current call remain monitor objects, not speculative canonical occurrences.
Scheduled information catalysts, scheduled producer-policy meetings, physical-risk windows and unscheduled physical shocks are different object classes.
A physical-risk window indicates elevated structural exposure only; actual storms, outages, attacks, shipping disruptions and production losses belong to the Shock/Live Intelligence layer.
Publication-time semantics must preserve source wording: EXACT_LOCAL_TIME, NOT_BEFORE_LOCAL_TIME, NORMAL_RELEASE_WINDOW and DATE_ONLY are not interchangeable.
High-frequency canonical releases may be BACKGROUND/ANALYST visibility and suppressed from the essential calendar without being removed from the registry.
Independent commodity/agricultural releases sharing a timestamp retain independent provenance and may be render-clustered.
An authoritative recurring release rule may generate future occurrences only through the horizon for which all holiday/exception inputs are authoritative.
Market-sensitive information releases are not encoded as directional price predictions; observed market response is populated only after the event.
Observed physical phenomena enter a shock-candidate screen before promotion to the Live Shock Register.
A named storm, outage, attack or disruption is not automatically a systemically material shock.
Risk-window linkage supplies context only; it must never mutate the risk window into the observed shock.
Absence of materiality evidence is not evidence of zero impact; use MATERIALITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED when evidence is insufficient.
Calendar rendering of shock candidates is prohibited. Only promoted live shocks may create alert/intelligence surfaces, and even then they remain distinct from scheduled calendar occurrences.

Shock promotion must cite observed transmission evidence such as production loss, port closure, power outage, transport interruption, policy response, casualty/displacement scale, or defensible market response.
A physical conference complex may contain multiple legally distinct treaty-body sessions; shared dates/venue do not merge legal identities.
Conference-complex grouping is a display and contextual relationship, not a canonical event merge.
Assessment-report timing can be confirmed at month, half-year or year precision without inventing an approval-session date.
Recently completed major environmental conferences may be retained as historical context anchors without re-entering the forward calendar population.
Scientific assessment products, treaty negotiations and physical climate hazards remain separate analytical object classes.
Trade-policy announcement date, legal adoption/publication date, customs effective date and later review/expiry date are distinct temporal facts.
A tariff or sanctions measure already in force before the forward reference horizon may remain a historical policy anchor while future review/expiry obligations become canonical forward milestones.
A WTO dispute consultation start may generate a conditional panel-request eligibility boundary, but not a scheduled panel request.
A sanctions expiry date is represented as an expiry/review boundary rather than an assertion that sanctions will terminate.
A trade negotiation can be CONFIRMED at month precision while the exact meeting day remains TBC.
Physical chokepoint disruption belongs to the Shock/Live Intelligence layer; it must not be turned into a recurring calendar event.
Trade-measure trackers are monitoring/provenance sources, not automatic canonical-event generators.
Technology-governance dates distinguish legal application, compliance/reporting onset, review/report deadlines, licence-application deadlines and authorisation-expiry boundaries.
A review deadline is not the same as publication of a review report; the deadline is canonical even if the report is published earlier.
An authorisation that expires absent subsequent notice is a conditional expiry boundary and must remain under source monitoring.
Cyber incident reporting obligations are regulatory milestones; actual cyber incidents remain Shock/Live Intelligence objects.
A recurring or expected cyber-rulemaking process does not become a canonical compliance date until the final legal instrument establishes one.
AI regulatory milestones are classified by the specific obligation/use-case layer rather than treating an entire AI statute as one date.
Regional technology-policy anchors may be retained even when already effective, while uncertain future implementation/grace periods remain monitor-only.
Technology and semiconductor policy must preserve geopolitical/industrial-policy relevance without encoding a directional market or geopolitical claim.
Cross-domain interaction records are analytical links, not canonical event mutations.
Temporal coincidence, structural connection, policy-response context and observed transmission are distinct interaction classes.
An interaction edge must state whether it is causal, mechanistic, contextual or merely temporal; default is NOT_A_CAUSAL_CLAIM.
Active shocks can raise the analytical priority of scheduled information releases without implying the release caused or was caused by the shock.
Regulatory overlap between regimes can be represented even when neither regime is causally upstream of the other.
Interaction edges never pre-populate observed market response; market reaction remains an observation linked after the event.
Alternative explanations are mandatory for any promoted observed association or causal hypothesis.
P0 metadata migration may alter only region, visibility_tier and universal category aliases when deterministic; event identity, timing, source provenance, certainty and lifecycle are protected.
Broad-region migration maps multi-region jurisdictions to Cross-regional / Global; it never assigns region by first place-name.
China is a collection programme across universal categories, not a standalone event category.
Health-governance meetings, pandemic-treaty negotiations and observed outbreaks are separate object classes.

WHO regional committee sessions remain region-specific governance records; a regional committee that is legally the same meeting as another named governing body is one occurrence with governance aliases, not duplicate events.
Actual outbreaks, PHEIC declarations and operational health emergencies route to Live Intelligence/Shock screening rather than recurring calendar series.
A potential or TBC IHR committee meeting remains a monitor until WHO confirms the date.
Existing cross-domain health events already in another canonical series are linked, not duplicated.
Coverage-correction population is driven by documented gaps, not equal country quotas.
When a recurring series is newly admitted for regional correction, populate all remaining occurrences in the current calendar year, then stop unless the next-year horizon is analytically necessary.
A published future-year schedule may be registered as authoritative yet deliberately deferred from canonical population to prevent schedule-rich domains from dominating the registry.

Multi-day central-bank decision forums can be one canonical decision-process occurrence where the source treats the days as one integrated meeting; do not multiply records solely for press conferences/minutes during a correction tranche.
Legal budget deadlines are canonical deadlines, not claims that submission/approval occurs exactly at the deadline.

Regional correction is assessed against the country's total cross-domain holdings, including existing elections, health, trade and institutions, rather than requiring each correction tranche to have equal domain counts.
Copyright/reuse permission and automated website-access permission are separate source-governance fields.
Public-domain or open-licence content does not by itself authorise unlimited automated crawling.
Where an institution provides an official feed/API/calendar surface, monitoring should prefer it over HTML scraping.
Non-commercial reuse permission is insufficient for a platform-independent production dependency unless commercial/redistribution status is separately resolved.
Legacy `Asia` and `Oceania` region aliases are retired; region vocabulary is canonicalised while jurisdiction is preserved unchanged.
Region is an analytical/display classification and must never replace or weaken canonical jurisdiction.
Earnings season is a derived reporting-density overlay, never a canonical event occurrence.
A statutory filing deadline, an issuer-announced results date, an actual earnings release and an actual periodic regulatory filing are separate temporal facts.
Issuer reporting occurrence identity is stable across reschedules and is based on issuer + fiscal period + report scope/type, not the announced date.
Forward issuer timing is tiered: confirmed issuer date > model-estimated historical cadence > statutory deadline constraint. A deadline alone is never treated as the expected actual release date.
Observed U.S. earnings-announcement density should preferentially identify Form 8-K Item 2.02 events separately from 10-Q/10-K filing density.
Reporting-density windows are calibrated empirically; arbitrary start/end thresholds are prohibited before backtesting.
Default cohort weighting is equal issuer count. Market-cap weighting requires rights-cleared market-cap data.
Index-based cohorts are optional and require explicit constituency-rights clearance; proprietary index membership must not become a hidden dependency.
Commercial earnings calendars may be used only as optional external validation and never as canonical provenance or a production dependency.
Issuer IR pages may be primary sources for forward dates but must be individually or programmatically rights/robots reviewed before automated retrieval.
Reporting regimes are versioned because filing deadlines and reporting frequency can change over time.
A change in regulatory reporting frequency or filer classification updates regime applicability; it does not mutate historical reporting occurrences.
For EDGAR filings, regulatory acceptance timestamp, official filing date and public-availability timestamp are distinct concepts.
EDGAR acceptance time may be used as an information-system timing proxy but must not be labelled exact public dissemination time.
When a filing is accepted after the SEC cutoff and receives the next business day's official filing date, both facts are preserved.
Density analysis must state which timestamp basis it uses; acceptance-based and official-filing-date density are different observational series.
The primary U.S. earnings-density calibration cohort is regulator-defined from SEC domestic-form periodic filers, not a proprietary market index.
Historical calibration must avoid current-listing survivorship bias: current SEC ticker/exchange files may support live display cohorts but do not define the historical calibration universe.
Each observation period receives a point-in-time cohort vintage constructed only from filings available before the observation cutoff.
Primary cohort eligibility is based on a qualifying Form 10-K in a trailing lookback window; foreign-private-issuer 20-F/6-K behaviour is modelled separately.
A recurring Item 2.02 reporter cohort may be derived only from prior-period Item 2.02 history and is a secondary analytical cohort, never a hidden eligibility filter.
Daily earnings density deduplicates first by accession number and then by issuer-day so one issuer cannot inflate a day by submitting multiple Item 2.02 filings.
Density is normalized by eligible cohort size to make historical periods comparable as the SEC registrant universe changes.
Peak detection and season-boundary calibration use training periods only; held-out periods are not used to choose parameters.
The system may render a density curve and peak markers before any season-boundary rule is admitted.
A named earnings-season window remains prohibited unless a parameter set passes held-out stability, coverage, compactness and non-overlap gates.
Bulk/API unavailability in a runtime is an execution limitation, not permission to substitute a commercial calendar or web-scraped approximation.
A source may remain valid historical provenance while being rejected as the future production-monitoring route.
Jurisdictional distribution restrictions can disqualify an otherwise authoritative source from production monitoring for the user's location.
Production source replacement must not rewrite historical occurrence provenance; monitoring route and evidentiary source identity are separate.
Open/public-domain/CC-licensed content does not automatically imply unrestricted automated access.
Regional correction may prioritise undercovered non-monetary domains even when a country's central-bank calendar is source-ready.
Financial-stability policy decisions and financial-stability reports are distinct canonical occurrences from monetary-policy decisions.
A budget commencement date is an implementation milestone distinct from parliamentary passage or royal assent.
A statutory budget-submission or autógrafa deadline is not an assertion that action occurs precisely at the deadline.
Country coverage repair is evaluated by domain mix as well as record count; source-ready monetary calendars may be deliberately deferred to avoid schedule-rich-domain dominance.
The Source/Change Monitor is a staging and review layer; it cannot mutate canonical occurrences directly.
FETCH → SNAPSHOT → PARSE → ASSERT → MATCH → DIFF → REVIEW → COMMIT → RENDER is enforced as the monitoring pipeline.
Every source snapshot carries a completeness contract; absence from a query-scoped/windowed feed is not evidence of cancellation or deletion.
Cancellation requires an explicit authoritative cancellation assertion or equivalent verified source status.
A changed date/time updates the same matched occurrence only after review; it never creates a duplicate merely because the schedule moved.
A newly discovered source item becomes a discovery candidate, not a canonical occurrence, until series/identity and source assertions pass review.
Source/endpoint failure changes source health only and must produce zero canonical mutation.
Title changes are weak evidence; stable source locators, series semantics, reference period and timing context outrank raw title string matching.
Machine-generated monitor verdict text must derive from structured validation/diff state; hard-coded PASS/FAIL prose is prohibited.
A production-monitoring source can differ from the historical primary provenance source for an occurrence.
Cross-source corroboration does not rewrite the primary source assertion or occurrence identity.
A second authoritative source repeating an indicative schedule does not automatically upgrade PROVISIONAL to CONFIRMED; the confirmation basis must itself be stronger.
Source-route replacement is a monitoring operation, not a canonical event mutation.
Semantic enrichment from a replacement route may be stored in monitor assertions without forcing a title rewrite when the existing canonical label remains substantively correct.
Monitoring rollout is staged by source rights, endpoint permission, parser readiness, runtime health and canonical dependency—not by source count.
A high canonical-dependency source with unresolved rights remains a hold regardless of importance.
PILOT_VALIDATED means monitor assertions/diffs can be generated; it does not authorise automatic canonical commits.
Monitoring priority score orders work within a readiness class and must not override a rights or licence hold.
A recurring-rule source is monitored as a rule plus exception set, not as a collection of unrelated scraped dates.
A change to a standard recurrence rule can generate multiple future diff candidates, but no bulk canonical mutation is allowed without review.
Holiday exceptions outrank the standard recurrence rule for the affected occurrence only.
Absence of a future holiday exception is not permission to infer one; population stops at the last horizon where the rule and known exceptions are sufficient.
Publication wording such as 'after 10:30' is preserved as a not-before semantic rather than converted to an exact 10:30 timestamp.
Automatic monitor commits remain disabled; a reviewed canonical commit is a distinct explicit operation after MATCH/DIFF/REVIEW.
A completed statistical release may upgrade certainty from PROVISIONAL to CONFIRMED while changing lifecycle from PLANNED to COMPLETED on the same occurrence.
Observed statistical values belong in the Observation/Live Intelligence layer and are linked to the completed occurrence; they are not embedded as calendar timing fields.
A reviewed canonical commit must record old/new values, approving assertion, review basis, commit timestamp and protected-field integrity checks.
A reviewed commit cannot alter occurrence_id, series_id, historical source identity, jurisdiction or event class unless the review explicitly authorises an identity/schema migration.
Market response remains null until separately observed; publication of a statistic does not imply a market reaction.
Institution-wide rights may be inherited by multiple source records only when the source content falls within the same terms regime.

Where an institution's official-document copyright notice and general website terms differ materially, production monitoring uses the more conservative classification until a source-specific route is identified.
A paid/non-CC analytical product can still supply manually curated public schedule facts without authorising ingestion of the underlying licensed report/data.
Canonical provenance is preserved when a source is placed on a future production-monitoring hold.
An authoritative source calendar may expose more releases than WORLD SIGNALS chooses to canonicalise; discovery is not automatic admission.
A source monitor must separate canonical matches from non-canonical discovery candidates.
Machine-friendly official feeds (ICS/RSS/API) are preferred to HTML when available and rights-compatible, but unsupported runtime content types do not justify an alternate commercial source.
An authoritative expected window such as 'autumn 2026' remains a monitor/window object unless an exact occurrence date is independently warranted.
A historical official date-move announcement may be used as a real regression fixture for parser/diff logic without mutating current canonical occurrences.
A source's factual authority does not override explicit prohibitions on shared-database storage or systematic automated collection.
Where official texts/data are public domain but the surrounding website terms are more restrictive, production monitoring must use a route clearly within the public-domain scope or obtain permission.
Joint institutional events inherit the most restrictive unresolved source route until a dedicated authorised feed/API is identified.
Public API permission for one institutional data product does not automatically authorise scraping a separate schedule webpage.
Rolling operational source pages require an explicit feed/window completeness scope; disappearance after the operational window is not cancellation evidence.

Source-detail enrichment (amount, ISIN, settlement date) may attach to monitor assertions without creating separate canonical occurrences unless the project separately defines those milestones as analytically material.
A future TBA row on an authoritative schedule is a hard population horizon boundary; historical cadence cannot fill beyond it.
A release calendar that includes related lower-priority statistics may generate discovery candidates without expanding the canonical registry automatically.
Authoritative discovery is necessary but insufficient for canonical admission.
Discovery review weighs intrinsic/systemic importance, unique information content, cross-domain utility, source readiness, marginal geographic/domain value, cadence load and duplication.
A candidate may be intrinsically important yet deferred when its marginal contribution worsens a documented coverage imbalance.
DEFERRED_FOR_COVERAGE_BALANCE means the source/item remains monitored and may be reconsidered after coverage re-audit; it is not a judgment that the signal is unimportant.
Source-detail fields and settlement mechanics are not promoted to standalone events unless a separate event ontology establishes independent analytical materiality.
A detailed authoritative calendar may still assert PROVISIONAL timing when the institution itself says future dates may change.
Schedule specificity and certainty are separate: exact day/time does not imply CONFIRMED status.
For sovereign auctions, a broad/monthly auction calendar and a later instrument-specific auction announcement are distinct evidence strengths for the same stable occurrence.
An instrument-specific announcement may confirm the occurrence without creating a second event; issue amount, issue date, maturity and reopening/new-issue detail remain assertion metadata.
A related release series exposed on the same official schedule, such as Tokyo CPI, remains a discovery candidate until coverage governance admits it.
A month/season window in an authoritative schedule remains a monitor object when no exact date is supplied.
Government or central-bank status is never treated as an implied open licence.
If an institution distinguishes designated public data from ordinary website content, a schedule page is not presumed to belong to the public-data class without evidence.
When an official law service provides a programmatic open-data API, that API should replace HTML scraping for production monitoring.
Failure to locate sufficiently clear reuse/automation terms results in a production hold, not an inferred permission.
Internal organisational-use permission is not equivalent to permission for external redistribution or a platform-independent production service.
Derived legal-deadline occurrences are monitored by tracking the operative rule inputs and re-running the derivation, not by scraping the derived date as if it were separately published.
A legal-rule amendment creates a re-derivation review candidate for every affected future occurrence; it does not silently rewrite dates.
Official open-data/API access should preserve the exact Korean source text/version identifiers used in the derivation.
An English translation may assist interpretation but the operative Korean legal text/version remains the authoritative rule basis where the translation itself disclaims legal authority.
A legal rule can remain unchanged even when its API/page version metadata changes; semantic rule hashes and clause extraction are therefore distinct from transport hashes.
The next monitor pilot is selected using dependency, source readiness, domain diversity and geographic value rather than canonical dependency count alone.
A very high-dependency source may be deferred when its rights or operational route is weaker than a lower-dependency but more diverse source.
Pilot-source count is not itself a production-readiness metric; heterogeneity of proven monitor behaviours matters.
Monitoring readiness treats non-commercial-only reuse permission as a rights hold for platform-independent production, even where internal/manual research use is permitted.
Ranking functions must never override source-governance classifications; a candidate must first pass the readiness gate before scoring.
Certainty of a rule-derived occurrence cannot exceed the certainty of the date-bearing anchor on which the derivation depends.
A publication rule can be authoritative while a derived future occurrence remains PROVISIONAL because its anchor date is tentative.
Monitor assertions are field-scoped: a source that asserts only a date or rule must not erase or downgrade unrelated canonical fields.
A failed or runtime-blocked endpoint with unknown snapshot completeness produces source-health state only and zero canonical event mutation.

Reviewed batch commits are permitted only when every affected occurrence shares the same deterministic rule defect, stable identity is preserved, and the commit ledger records each occurrence separately.
Branch reconciliation must prefer the exact parent checkpoint over semantic or heuristic rebinding whenever that checkpoint becomes available.
A branch-side lifecycle candidate that does not map to an existing canonical occurrence is reclassified as a completed non-canonical discovery rather than forced into the registry.
Eurostat source-native certainty is weekly: planning for the following week is confirmed each Friday; all longer-horizon planning remains provisional.
Exact date/time and certainty remain orthogonal: a precise Eurostat annual-calendar date outside the frozen weekly horizon is PROVISIONAL.
A branch-recovery correction may supersede a branch-only candidate classification without altering historical parent provenance.
A statutory deadline occurrence may become COMPLETED before its deadline without moving the canonical deadline date; completion evidence is recorded separately.
When evidence proves only that an obligation was completed by a given date, store completion_verified_by_date rather than inventing an exact actual completion date.
A source-supported month window may be upgraded in place to an exact civil date when the operative legal text later supplies that date.
A rule-derived procedural date must use the rule's legally relevant anchor; publication/circulation date cannot substitute for receipt/request date unless the rule says so.
When the legally relevant anchor date is unresolved but bounded by authoritative evidence, downgrade an exact derived date to an evidence-bounded window rather than choosing a preferred day.

Conflicting precision from joint and unilateral official sources is stored as a source-precision disagreement; the joint assertion remains canonical unless superseded by a stronger joint/competent source.
Financial-stability coverage is a distinct canonical domain from monetary-policy decisions even when the issuing institution is a central bank.
A prudential-standard effective date is an implementation milestone, not a policy-announcement date.
A source-confirmed month of publication may be canonical with MONTH precision and CONFIRMED certainty; no day is inferred.
Financial-stability population must add unique systemic-risk/prudential information rather than duplicate central-bank meeting calendars.
Source rights/readiness is part of candidate admission; source-ready alternatives are preferred over equally useful sources with production-rights holds.
A geographic coverage gap is not sufficient reason to admit an event; regional correction requires independent event materiality, authoritative timing and source-governance fitness.
Rights or licence terms are never inherited merely because two sources share a parent institution, hostname or brand; inheritance requires explicit scope evidence.
A source-supported future date may remain a frontier candidate when source rights or event ontology are unresolved.
A historical publication cadence is not a forward schedule. A publication archive without a future assertion cannot generate a future canonical occurrence.
Health/Biosecurity events sourced from rights-held WHO webpages remain valid curated canonical provenance but are manual-verification dependencies until an authorised monitoring route is established.
Manual verification priority is operational metadata, not event importance.

A tax-reform transition phase may be represented by a canonical implementation-boundary occurrence when the operative law specifies an exact commencement date and the reform has system-wide political-economic transmission.
A narrow administrative sub-rule is not substituted for the broader reform milestone when the operative legal framework supports a system-level boundary.
Creative Commons reuse permission and automated retrieval permission remain separate; a source can support canonical curated provenance while endpoint polling remains under operational review.
WHO general website terms are applied to WHO-hosted governance pages as the Organization's stated website-use regime; they do not authorise a platform-independent commercial production monitor.
A public-health data API or dataset licence cannot be substituted for a governance-event schedule unless that route actually supplies the event assertions being monitored.
Machine-readable transport does not change source-rights classification: an iCalendar export is not an independent licence.
A user-facing 'Add to iCal' export is not assumed to be a stable subscription feed or production polling endpoint.
WHO calendar-export surfaces may assist manual verification and parser prototyping while WHO production automation remains rights-held.
A future WHO monitoring promotion requires either explicit permission, a separately licensed event feed/API, or terms that clearly authorize the intended production use.
Canonical occurrence region is a scalar controlled-vocabulary value, not a one-element array.
`Australia & Pacific` is normalized to the established canonical region `Oceania / Pacific`.
Geographic normalization is deterministic metadata hygiene only: occurrence identity, timing, lifecycle, source and analytical importance are protected from mutation.
Coverage audits must reject mixed region field types before drawing geographic-balance conclusions.
Passing the scheduled date is not evidence that an event completed; lifecycle completion requires an authoritative post-event assertion.
A rights-held source may support manual reviewed lifecycle completion without becoming an automated production-monitor dependency.
A stale or pre-release official web index after an event date is a source-health/reverification condition, not permission to infer completion.
Policy-decision values belong in the Observation/Live Intelligence layer rather than the calendar timing record.
Observed market response remains null unless separately researched; a rate hold or change is not itself evidence of market impact.
A statutory 'before midnight on DATE' boundary is represented as a civil-date deadline with end-of-civil-date semantics; no synthetic 23:59:59 timestamp is created.
An annual legal deadline is eligible for current-cycle canonical population only when the corresponding real-world process is active or otherwise analytically relevant within the population horizon.
Open-data inventory/API access may monitor legal instrument presence/version while the operative legal-text webpage remains the manually verified authoritative clause source.
Licence terms for an open-data inventory are not automatically imputed to separate HTML legal-text renderings.
Regional correction remains additive only when the new occurrence supplies genuinely distinct fiscal, regulatory, institutional or systemic information.
Regional institutional importance does not override non-commercial-only website terms for platform-independent production monitoring.
Existing canonical provenance is not invalidated when its future automated monitoring route is placed on a rights hold.
A known host year or chairship is not an exact summit date; TBC institutional occurrences remain TBC until the competent institution publishes stronger timing.
A sectoral ministerial can remain a frontier candidate even when exact and analytically useful if source-governance and marginal-calendar-value gates are unresolved.
Canonical provenance fitness and automated-monitoring permission are separate source-governance dimensions.

An authoritative source may support manually curated factual event metadata even when automated production retrieval is rights-held, provided the permitted-use scope supports that manual/reference use.
A rights-held automated route does not invalidate a canonical occurrence; it changes verification mode and monitoring readiness.
A future implementation date taken from an official planning timetable remains PROVISIONAL until enactment/promulgation or another competent source confirms the operative date.
An official parliamentary programme may support CONFIRMED scheduled timing even when future automated polling of that website is prohibited; subsequent changes still require manual re-verification.
Source rights must record both canonical_provenance_use and automated_monitoring_use so calendar-population and monitoring decisions cannot be conflated.

A current authoritative data-product page can verify publication completion even when the publication landing/index page lags, provided the data product explicitly carries the current release date/reference period.

Source-surface hierarchy must distinguish publication index, underlying data product, schedule/rule page and archive; disagreement is a source-health condition, not necessarily an event-content conflict.
A discontinuous legislative session is not rendered as one continuous date span unless the institution actually sits continuously.
For a provisionally scheduled multi-phase legislative session, the canonical event may represent the opening milestone while phase windows are preserved as schedule metadata.

An official government or legislative report that explicitly permits republication with source attribution may support curated factual provenance; automated retrieval remains a separate operational review.
A provisional official programme remains PROVISIONAL even when its start date is exact.
Attention, consumption and mobility regimes are derived overlays, not canonical event occurrences.
A public holiday or cultural observance anchor does not itself assert a travel, retail, freight, liquidity or market effect.
Effect windows require empirical calibration or current observational evidence; intuitive pre/post buffers are prohibited.
Non-contiguous holiday clusters remain non-contiguous anchors rather than being silently converted into continuous closures.
Commercial labels such as Black Friday may be rule-derived attention anchors, but sales intensity is an observation/model output rather than an intrinsic property of the date.

Religious observance dates that remain contingent on astronomical observation or competent religious declaration retain PROVISIONAL certainty even when an administrative calendar prints an exact date.
Mega-event attention is separated from the scheduled event itself and from any claimed economic, security, tourism or market transmission.
Observed market response and causal attribution remain separate from overlay intensity.
Sectoral ministerial meetings may be canonical international-institution occurrences when they have material cross-domain policy relevance; not every working-group meeting is admitted.
APEC main-site factual schedule metadata may support manual curated provenance with attribution while automated production monitoring remains rights-held.
Overlay calibration sources live in a separate data-source registry from canonical event sources.
Calibration data rights, cadence, granularity, continuity and machine accessibility are separate admission dimensions.
Failure of the local execution environment to fetch a verified official dataset is an environment-ingestion fault, not a source-health fault.
An event-time diagnostic horizon is not an asserted behavioural effect window.
Where two calendar anchors are deterministically adjacent, a single outcome series cannot causally identify their separate effects without additional variation or independent data.
US Black Friday is always Thanksgiving +1 day; TSA air-travel data therefore calibrates a Thanksgiving mobility regime, not an independently identifiable Black Friday mobility effect.
Pandemic-disrupted years are not silently discarded; they are modeled as a separate structural-break regime.
A statutory fiscal-process deadline is a canonical boundary, not a prediction that the government or legislature will act on the last permissible day.
A standing legal deadline is populated for the next budget cycle only when authoritative evidence shows that cycle is active.
Written-law reuse status may support legal-rule provenance without implying reuse permission for the broader government website carrying corroborating process material.

When an official ministry page supplies a legal/procedural deadline but site-wide reuse terms are unresolved, curated factual provenance may remain manual while automated monitoring is held for endpoint/rights review.
An active legislative or budget process without an authoritative future passage/enactment date remains a frontier process object rather than receiving an invented deadline.

Overlay data acquisition is fail-closed: a verified official distribution that cannot be fetched in the current execution environment remains pending; no commercial or unofficial mirror may silently replace it.
A validation webpage is not automatically a calibration dataset. Temporal completeness and machine extraction must be demonstrated separately.
Monthly retail data are too coarse to identify a day-level Black Friday effect window, even if they are excellent macroeconomic data.
Monitoring automation readiness and canonical auto-commit readiness are separate gates.
A source may be pilot-validated for automated FETCH/PARSE/ASSERT/MATCH/DIFF while canonical commits remain review-only.
Manual-only rights-held sources can remain valid canonical provenance but cannot enter automated production monitoring through that route.
A source scoring/ranking system may operate only after the rights/automation gate has classified the route.

Automatic canonical commit requires evidence across real reschedules, cancellations, completions, certainty changes, source-surface conflicts and rollback behaviour; synthetic tests alone are insufficient.

The current reviewed-change history is rich in certainty corrections and completions but lacks a real current cancellation and a real current reschedule committed from the production monitor; automatic commit therefore remains closed.
Low-risk automation may generate review candidates but must not bypass REVIEW -> COMMIT.
Endpoint-route validity, source health and local execution-environment health are separate states.
A sandbox DNS/network failure cannot downgrade an authoritative source or imply that an official endpoint is unavailable.
An endpoint is not promoted to production-validated merely because its documentation and web-facing route are research-verified; the actual transport/parser path must execute successfully.
Machine-readable source routes may be transport-specific: SOAP search, REST document retrieval, RSS publication feeds and Socrata inventory APIs are distinct monitor types.
An open legal-instrument inventory can detect presence/status/version changes but cannot substitute for the operative legal clause when the dataset does not contain clause-level text.
A real historical reschedule already represented in canonical status history should receive an explicit provenance change-ledger object rather than remain only in prose notes.
A historical reschedule reconciliation does not count as a live-monitor reschedule commit if the canonical record already contains the new date before the monitor run.
Explicit cancellations discovered outside the canonical population do not count toward the automatic-commit cancellation gate merely because they are convenient test cases.
Source-surface conflict resolution uses competence, specificity, chronology and current-state authority rather than majority voting across webpages.
A superseded official announcement remains valid historical provenance but cannot override a later competent official revision.
An event-specific official page outranks a generic institutional directory when their timing fields conflict.
An unverified or unofficial host-branded portal cannot override a competent official institution or host-government announcement.
A coarse institutional calendar range cannot override an event-specific sitting schedule for discontinuous or non-daily proceedings.
Real historical reschedule assertions may be used to exercise apply-validate-rollback-reapply transaction logic without being mislabelled as prospective monitor detection.
Transaction replay on real historical evidence strengthens commit safety evidence but does not satisfy the separate requirement for a live prospective reschedule.
A legal-triggered reschedule should preserve both the superseded dates and the stated legal trigger when the trigger is supported by the competent authority or a contemporaneous report quoting it.
Source-health state and event-state are independent: source degradation cannot create, cancel, complete, reschedule or downgrade a canonical occurrence by itself.
A source-health incident may quarantine a transport or surface while permitting an alternate official surface to continue evidence collection.
Recovery requires a positive authoritative assertion from the recovered or alternate official surface; elapsed time or restored HTTP status alone is insufficient to mutate canonical event state.
Source-health incidents must record whether canonical mutation was blocked during degradation and whether any later reviewed event commit occurred only after event evidence recovered.
A lagging index with a current underlying official data product is a partial-surface degradation, not an institution-wide source outage.
An empty dynamic calendar conflicting with an authoritative full-year release document remains an unresolved surface-health incident; absence on the dynamic page is not cancellation evidence.
Source-health recovery can satisfy monitor-resilience evidence without satisfying separate prospective-reschedule or canonical-cancellation gates.
Controlled failure injection must operate on an isolated monitor/canonical clone and cannot share a mutable object with the production canonical registry.
A fetch failure yields no event assertion and therefore cannot produce cancellation, completion, certainty or timing mutation.
Parser output must pass schema, datetime and provenance validation before MATCH/DIFF; malformed parser output is quarantined before event-state comparison.
A syntactically valid but deliberately corrupted parsed value may generate a sandbox review candidate only when explicitly marked FAULT_INJECTION; automatic canonical commit remains prohibited.
Recovery requires re-reading a positive current authoritative assertion; restored parser health alone does not prove event state.
Protected canonical digests are computed before each injected fault and after recovery. Any protected-field drift fails the entire resilience gate.
A controlled failure-injection pass satisfies the monitor failure-containment requirement but does not provide evidence for prospective reschedule or cancellation commits.
Month-bounded seasonal risk windows preserve source-native month precision in year-qualified YYYY-MM season_phases[]; first/last civil days are never manufactured.
A multi-phase seasonal risk window preserves each authoritative non-contiguous phase independently and in order; gaps are not collapsed into a continuous span.
For month-bounded seasonal windows, start_local/end_local, UTC timestamps and date_earliest/date_latest remain empty because those fields would imply day or clock precision the source did not assert.

Calendar/index rendering may derive an internal month-start sort proxy from season_phases[] but that proxy is never canonical timing and must not be displayed, exported or written back as an event date.

A dynamic annual season outlook is an information assertion about expected timing and remains separate from a stable PHYSICAL_RISK_WINDOW occurrence unless the authority explicitly establishes a canonical bounded window.
